# Design of this implementation

Stack-specific guidance for this implementation of the app: its stack, layout and conventions.
Read it with `AGENTS.md`, which has the working rules and how the app is tested.

*The following is Angular's official best-practices rules file, included verbatim from
<https://angular.dev/assets/context/best-practices.md>. It is part of the Angular
architecture.*

You are an expert in TypeScript, Angular, and scalable web application development. You write functional, maintainable, performant, and accessible code following Angular and TypeScript best practices.

## TypeScript Best Practices

- Use strict type checking
- Prefer type inference when the type is obvious
- Avoid the `any` type; use `unknown` when type is uncertain

## Angular Best Practices

- Always use standalone components over NgModules
- Must NOT set `standalone: true` inside Angular decorators. It's the default in Angular v20+.
- Do NOT set `changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush` explicitly. `OnPush` is the default in Angular v22+.
- Use signals for state management
- Implement lazy loading for feature routes
- Do NOT use the `@HostBinding` and `@HostListener` decorators. Put host bindings inside the `host` object of the `@Component` or `@Directive` decorator instead
- Use `NgOptimizedImage` for all static images.
  - `NgOptimizedImage` does not work for inline base64 images.

## Accessibility Requirements

- It MUST pass all AXE checks.
- It MUST follow all WCAG AA minimums, including focus management, color contrast, and ARIA attributes.

### Components

- Keep components small and focused on a single responsibility
- Use `input()` and `output()` functions instead of decorators
- Use `model()` for two-way bound properties with `[(prop)]` syntax instead of pairing `input()` with `output()`
- Use `computed()` for derived state
- Use `linkedSignal()` for state derived from multiple reactive sources that must stay synchronized
- Prefer inline templates for small components
- Prefer Signal Forms (`@angular/forms/signals`) for new forms. They are stable in Angular v22+ and provide signal-based state, type-safe field access, and schema-based validation
- When not using Signal Forms, prefer Reactive forms instead of Template-driven ones
- Do NOT use `ngClass`, use `class` bindings instead
- Do NOT use `ngStyle`, use `style` bindings instead
- Do NOT import `CommonModule`, import only the directives and pipes the template uses, such as `AsyncPipe` or `DatePipe`
- When using external templates/styles, use paths relative to the component TS file.

## State Management

- Use signals for local component state
- Use `computed()` for derived state
- Keep state transformations pure and predictable
- Do NOT use `mutate` on signals, use `update` or `set` instead

## Templates

- Keep templates simple and avoid complex logic
- Use native control flow (`@if`, `@for`, `@switch`) instead of `*ngIf`, `*ngFor`, `*ngSwitch`
- Use the async pipe to handle observables
- Do not assume globals like (`new Date()`) are available.

## Services

- Design services around a single responsibility
- Use the `providedIn: 'root'` option for singleton services
- Prefer the `@Service` decorator over `@Injectable({providedIn: 'root'})` for new singleton services (Angular v22+)
- Use the `inject()` function instead of constructor injection

---

## Spring

This is a standard Spring Boot application, built with conventional Spring MVC
(`@RestController` request handling, a service layer, Spring Data / JPA persistence, and Bean
Validation). Follow ordinary Spring conventions and idioms throughout. Spring's reference
documentation is the guidance for the server: Spring Boot
<https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/4.1/reference/> and Spring Framework
<https://docs.spring.io/spring-framework/reference/>.

import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import { resetAndSeed } from '../support/seed';

// A region can set a statutory grace period (settings.regionGraceDays, region -> days). A client in
// that region without a grace period of their own gets it instead of the usual 7 days, for when
// their invoices, instalments and released retention become overdue and when late interest starts.
test.describe('regional grace periods', () => {
  test("gives a region's statutory grace period", { tag: '@core' }, async ({ page }) => {
    await resetAndSeed({
      asOf: '2026-03-20',
      settings: { lateInterestRate: 12, regionGraceDays: { NY: 30, OR: 0 } },
      clients: [
        { id: 1, name: 'Acme Ltd', email: 'ops@acme.example', region: 'NY' },
        { id: 2, name: 'Globex Corp', email: 'billing@globex.example', region: 'OR' },
        { id: 3, name: 'Initech', email: 'ap@initech.example', region: 'NY', graceDays: 3 },
      ],
      invoices: [
        { id: 1, clientId: 1, status: 'SENT', issueDate: '2026-02-01', dueDate: '2026-03-01',
          lineItems: [{ id: 1, description: 'Build', qty: 1, unitPrice: 1000 }] },
        { id: 2, clientId: 2, status: 'SENT', issueDate: '2026-02-01', dueDate: '2026-03-01',
          lineItems: [{ id: 2, description: 'Build', qty: 1, unitPrice: 1000 }] },
        { id: 3, clientId: 3, status: 'SENT', issueDate: '2026-02-01', dueDate: '2026-03-01',
          lineItems: [{ id: 3, description: 'Build', qty: 1, unitPrice: 1000 }] },
      ],
    });
    await page.goto('/');

    // New York gives 30 days: due 2026-03-01, not overdue until after 2026-03-31
    await page.getByTestId('client-row-1').click();
    await expect(page.getByTestId('invoice-row-1').getByTestId('invoice-status')).toHaveText('Sent');
    await page.getByTestId('invoice-row-1').click();
    await expect(page.getByTestId('invoice-interest')).toHaveText('$0.00');
    // Oregon gives none: interest from the due date, 19 days on 1,000.00 at 12%
    await page.getByTestId('client-row-2').click();
    await expect(page.getByTestId('invoice-row-2').getByTestId('invoice-status')).toHaveText('Overdue');
    await page.getByTestId('invoice-row-2').click();
    await expect(page.getByTestId('invoice-panel-number')).toHaveText(await page.getByTestId('invoice-row-2').getByTestId('invoice-number').innerText());
    await expect(page.getByTestId('invoice-interest')).toHaveText('$6.35');
    await expect(page.getByTestId('client-row-2').getByTestId('client-overdue')).toHaveText('$1,006.35');
    // a client's own grace still wins: Initech's 3 days, 16 days of interest
    await page.getByTestId('client-row-3').click();
    await page.getByTestId('invoice-row-3').click();
    await expect(page.getByTestId('invoice-panel-number')).toHaveText(await page.getByTestId('invoice-row-3').getByTestId('invoice-number').innerText());
    await expect(page.getByTestId('invoice-panel-status')).toHaveText('Overdue');
    await expect(page.getByTestId('invoice-interest')).toHaveText('$5.35');
  });
});

content.text: The test passes. Checking for leftover formatting from the edit.

I've added grace periods per region. `bin/e2e` passes, including the check that replays earlier test data.

**What changed**
- **Stored data:** a client's grace period is now optional. A new migration, `V63__region_grace_days.sql`, lets `client.grace_days` be empty and removes its default of 7. Each region's grace period is stored as a workspace setting named `region_grace_days_<region>`, the same way per-region interest caps are already stored. A new `RegionGrace` service reads and writes these settings.
- **How grace is worked out:** `Invoice` now takes the client's own grace period, falls back to their region's, and then to the usual 7 days. Overdue status, instalments, released retention and late interest all get their grace period from this one place, so they all pick up the region's value.
- **Client:** `Client`, `ClientController` and the front end now allow a client to have no grace period. A new client created without one gets no default, so the region's grace period applies to them. The form's hint text says this too.
- **Test endpoints:** seeding accepts `settings.regionGraceDays`, with each value checked to be 0–30 days, and reads it back. A client's `graceDays` is only returned when one is stored.

**Two things to check**
- **Existing clients with exactly 7 days are cleared.** The migration sets their grace period to empty, so they now follow their region. Until now, 7 was what every client got when none was set, so "chose 7" and "never set" can't be told apart. Nothing changes for them until a region grace period is set. If you'd rather keep their 7 days, delete the `UPDATE` line in V63.
- **There's no screen to set a region's grace period.** The app has no workspace-settings screen, and the existing per-region tax rates and interest caps are also only set through stored data. I followed that and didn't build a new screen. Say if you want one.
